players.name: Nic Maddinson
players.bio:
Nic Maddinson is an attacking left-handed batter who has now twice been a shock inclusion in an Australian Test team, with almost a decade between opportunities.

Maddinson first burst onto the scene in the 2010-11 season when he made his List A and Sheffield shield debuts with NSW within days of each other. At 18 years old he became the youngest NSW player to score a century on first-class debut in his first Sheffield Shield match against South Australia at Adelaide Oval. (Kurtis Patterson would break this record a summer later).

He won his first Steve Waugh Medal as the NSW Blues' Player of the Year in 2015-16, having scored 380 runs at 63.33 in the One-Day Cup with a strike rate of 100.52, with two centuries. He was the only NSW player to feature in all 10 Shield matches that summer, his season highlighted by a superb 112 against Queensland at the SCG, as well as skippering the Blues in six Shield matches following an injury to Moises Henriques. Maddinson peeled off a century for Australia A against India A in Mackay in August 2016, and thrust himself into Test calculations after scoring the only ton of the match in NSW's Shield clash with Victoria in November 2016 on a turning SCG wicket. 

Even so, he was a shock inclusion in an overhaul of Australia's Test XI against South Africa in November 2016 following a nadir against the Proteas in Hobart, making his debut in Adelaide alongside Matthew Renshaw and Peter Handscomb. 

He played three Tests that summer, but struggled for consistency amid the spotlight thereafter, and lost his NSW contract in 2018, sparking a move to Melbourne later that year to try and force his way onto the Vics list through Premier Cricket performances.

He became arguably Victoria's most important batter across his six seasons with the state, scoring 2,785 Sheffield Shield runs at 50.64, including 10 centuries, before moving back to NSW ahead of the 2024-25 season.

Having been sidelined from cricket while he battled testicular cancer in 2025, he returned to play a handful of Big Bash games in early 2026. Back at full health, he was named NSW's Sheffield Shield skipper for 2026-27 under new coach Brad Haddin, then after hitting 126 against Victoria in a One-Day Cup game in late September he was a shock inclusion in Australia's Test squad on their 2026 tour of South Africa. At the time, Maddinson had not played a first-class game for 19 months.

players.name: Travis Head
players.didyouKnow: In 2015, Head was named captain of the Redbacks and at the age of 21 became the state's youngest captain of all time.
players.bio:
A former Hampshire scholar and Australia Under-19 representative, left-handed batter Travis Head had a golden run of form at the start of the 2013-14 season that led South Australia coach Darren Berry to describe him as a future Test player.

Alongside his batting prowess, Head was long touted as a leader-in-the-making when he led South Australia to their Under-19 National Championship title in 2012-13. His leadership skills were clearly admired as, at the remarkable age of 21, he was named the youngest captain of his state team.

In and out of the nation's Test and ODI sides across the first five years of his international career, Head cemented his spot as one of Australia's most important batters with an incredible 148-ball 152 at the Gabba in the opening Test of the 2021-22 Ashes.

He was awarded player of the match for his 163 in Australia's maiden World Test Championship triumph against India in 2023, and seized his chance as Aaron Finch's replacement to open the batting in the ODI side after his retirement in 2022.

Despite suffering a broken hand a few weeks out from the 2023 50-over World Cup in India, Head was deemed that important to Australia's chances that selectors opted to carry him through the first half of the tournament.

He duly delivered with a stunning 59-ball hundred in his first match of the tournament against New Zealand in Dharamsala, and finished the campaign with another player-of-the-match performance in the final as his 137 against India sealed a remarkable sixth ODI World Cup for the country.

Head has also had an illustrious career in the Big Bash League with the Adelaide Strikers, recording the club's first ever century along with leading them to their championship title in BBL|07, but it took until the 2023-24 summer for his to establish himself as a three-format player for Australia.

He won his first Allan Border Medal at the 2025 Australian Cricket Awards, presented the prize in the lobby of the Sri Lanka hotel where the Australian Test team was on tour.

An injury to Usman Khawaja saw Head make a surprise elevation to open the batting in the opening Test of the 2025-26 Ashes, and responded by peeling off an incredible 123 from just 83 balls. He remained as Test opener for the rest of the series, hitting two further centuries - in Adelaide and Sydney - and finishing the series with 629 runs at 62.90.

players.name: Scott Boland
players.bio:
In the space of four overs, Scott Boland made himself an instant hero with his unforgettable 6-7 on Test debut at his home ground the MCG against England in the 2021-22 Ashes.

That remarkable performance earnt him the Johnny Mullagh Medal, as well as a second Test in Sydney where he claimed figures of 7-66 across two innings. 

But it's easy to forget the toil the right-armer went through to earn his Baggy Green. The Victorian made his first-class debut in late 2011, before he had a breakout summer in 2013-14, taking 19 wickets from nine Sheffield Shield matches. His consistent form then carried over to the 2014-15 season, where he collected 25 wickets.

That led to him making his ODI debut against India in 2016 at the WACA, following impressive performances in Sheffield Shield and domestic one-day tournaments.

Boland's reliable performances for Victoria earned him a surprise call-up to Australia's Test squad, as a standby player for the Hobart Test against West Indies in 2015, however he was forced to wait until Boxing Day 2021 to make his debut in the Test arena and begin what has so far been a scarcely believable career.

Boland was also a member of the XI for Australia's first ever World Test Championship final victory, where he took five wickets in the win over India in June 2023.

In the third match of Frank Worrell Trophy series of 2025, Boland bookmarked his fabled career with another accomplishment by taking a Test hat-trick against the West Indies.

players.name: Marnus Labuschagne
players.didyouKnow: Labuschagne was part of Queensland's triumphant Sheffield Shield side in 2017/18, finishing the season as the competition's second-highest run-scorer
players.bio:
Born in South Africa, Marnus Labuschagne migrated with his family to Brisbane in 2004 and entered the Queensland Cricket underage system when he was 11.

The top-order batter made his first-class debut in the opening round of the 2014–15 Sheffield Shield campaign, aged 20, grinding out 83 runs against South Australia as an opener.

With just three List A games under his belt heading into the 2016-17 season, Labuschagne turned heads by being named Player of the Tournament for the 2016 Matador One-Day Cup, finishing with 273 runs at 45 to help steer the Bulls into the final.

The following season Labuschagne hit his straps in the red-ball arena, featuring in Queensland's triumphant Sheffield Shield side, and finishing the season as the competition's second-highest run-scorer with 795 runs at 39.75, including two hundreds.

Several months later, Labuschagne was awarded with Test cap No.455 on Australia's tour of the UAE in October 2018, making 0 and 13 on debut.

After losing and then regaining his spot in the following home summer, the right-hander's Test career really took off in 2019 when after an unexpected Ashes cameo (becoming Test cricket's first concussion substitute, replacing Steve Smith at Lord's) he ended up being the world's leading run-scorer in Tests for the calendar year. What followed was a dominant home season which included four centuries from five matches, including a double-century.

Arguably one of Labuschagne's best centuries came during the 2023 Ashes series, when the Queenslander held off a rampant England attack to score an invaluable 111 in Manchester, securing the draw that would retain the urn.

Labuschagne was initially left out of Australia's 15-man squad for the 2023 ODI World Cup in India, but an injury to Ashton Agar opened the door for the middle-order batter and he took it with both hands, playing every match of Australia's campaign and scoring a crucial 58 not out in the final.

The prolific batter played his 50th Test match in New Zealand in March 2024 with over 4,000 runs to his name in the format, having established himself as Australia's No.3 since that breakout Ashes campaign in 2019.

Form deserted him in 2024-25 and, after a makeshift stint as opener in Australia's 2025 World Test Championship Final defeat to South Africa, he was dropped from the Test side for the West Indies tour.

players.name: Steve Smith
players.birthPlace: St George Hospital, Kogarah, New South Wales
players.didyouKnow: Now a vital cog in Australia's batting unit, Smith initially made his name as a bowler -  He was New South Wales' leading wicket-taker in the 2007-08
players.bio:
A career that has seen him transform from full-time leg-spinner to one of the best batters in modern-day cricket, Steve Smith's story is one for the ages.

After making his first-class debut in 2008, Smith was given his Baggy Green two years later in a Test match against Pakistan at Lord's, where he batted at No.8 and took three wickets as the front-line spinner in Australia's win.

Later dropped from the Australian team due to a poor run at the 2010-11 Ashes, Smith turned to domestic cricket to regain form and confidence. After a recall to the Test side in 2013, he displayed extraordinary improvement, starting with his maiden Test ton at The Oval, later followed by centuries at Perth and Sydney during Australia's 5-0 whitewash in the 2013-14 Ashes.

Smith became Australia's 45th Test captain during the series against India in 2014-15, filling in for an injured Michael Clarke. It turned out to be a landmark series for him as he went onto post tons in all four Tests.

Reaching No.1 in the ICC Test batter rankings for the first time in June 2015, he was also awarded the Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy for ICC Cricketer of the Year the same year, and became the full-time Test captain following Clarke's retirement.

2017 was the year that his excellent form became astonishing, starting off with three Test tons while touring India and three more in the triumphant Ashes series the following summer, improving his Test batting average until it stood second only to Sir Donald Bradman.

However, the sandpaper scandal that erupted in Cape Town in March 2018 saw him stripped of the captaincy, banned from playing for 12 months and handed a two-year restriction from holding a leadership position in Australian cricket.

In his first Test back – the opening match of the 2019 Ashes series – he scored an incredible 144 in the first innings and an even better 142 in the second at Edgbaston to inspire Australia to victory, going on to dominate the series as Australia retained the Ashes.

Smith was returned to a formal leadership position in November 2021, named vice-captain to Pat Cummins. He captained Australia in the second Test of that summer's Ashes when Cummins was ruled out with Covid-19, and captained Australia in numerous Test and ODI matches since.

Australia's maiden appearance in the World Test Championship final in mid-2023 was tailor-made for Smith as he posted a memorable first-innings 121 as the Aussies lifted the mace for the first time. 

In November 2023, Smith added a third World Cup trophy to his illustrious resume (to go with the 2015 ODI and 2021 T20 World Cups) when he and Australia triumphed over India in the ODI tournament of that year.

He passed 11,000 Test runs during Australia's tour of South Africa in 2026.

players.name: Matt Renshaw
players.didyouKnow: In December 2018, Renshaw scored 345 for Toombul off 273 balls, with 38 fours and 12 sixes, a record for Brisbane senior cricket.
players.bio:
An Under-19 representative for Australia, Renshaw burst onto the domestic scene in December 2015 when struck an epic 170 against a strong NSW attack to become the youngest first-class century maker for Queensland. Born in Yorkshire, he was a family friend of England batter Joe Root as a youngster.

After his mammoth breakout innings, Renshaw finished his maiden Sheffield Shield campaign as Queensland's leading Shield run scorer with 738 at 43.41 in 2015-16. 

In 2017, Renshaw became the first Australian cricketer to make 500 Test runs before turning 21 years old which included a memorable 184 against Pakistan in Sydney. 

However, following his dream start a difficult six Tests in Asia (four in India, two in Bangladesh) and a barren start to the following Shield season saw Renshaw left out of the Aussie team for the 2017-18 Ashes series, with Cameron Bancroft preferred. 

Ironically, it was Renshaw who was called up to replace the suspended Bancroft during the ill-fated tour of South Africa in early 2018. 

A couple of lean seasons saw Renshaw move to the middle order, where he flourished during the Covid-affected 2020-21 summer, scoring 500 Shield runs at an average of 62.50. His one-day and T20 form also improved following his positional shift. 

A strong county campaign with Somerset in 2022 followed and ahead of the 2022-23 New Year's Test against South Africa, Renshaw was recalled to the Australian XI. 

The tall left-hander also played two Tests on Australia's unsuccessful tour to India in 2023. 

Two centuries for Australia A as opener saw him return to the top of the order for the 2023-24 Marsh Sheffield Shield season and 2024 County Championship season.

players.name: Alex Carey
players.didyouKnow: Alex Carey was captain of the Greater Western Sydney Giants in 2010, prior to them joining the AFL.
players.bio:
After starting out as a cricketer, Carey decided to pursue a career in Australian Rules football and as an 18-year-old was the inaugural captain and Best and Fairest Award winner for the newly formed Greater Western Sydney Giants in his first season. But Carey was axed by the club as they prepared to enter the top tier AFL competition in 2012, and was soon lured back to cricket by the South Australian Redbacks. There has been no looking back ever since.

Carey had long been highly regarded by South Australia, having played under-age cricket for the state.

Having returned to the state set-up he soon switched from full-time batter to wicketkeeper-batter and found form, taking the gloves full-time for the state in the 2015-16 summer. 

The left-hander played a big role in securing Adelaide Strikers' BBL|07 title win in 2017-18 – his incredible ton against the Hobart Hurricanes being a standout performance, and had narrowly missed out on Test selection for that summer's Ashes series. But his terrific run of form earned him his ODI & T20I debuts early in 2018, with the wicketkeeper soon donning the role of vice-captain in both formats, including at the 2019 ODI World Cup in England where he epitomised Aussie grit to bat on, bloodied and bandaged, after being struck on the chin during the semi-final. 

His Test call up came in the 2021-22 summer to replace Tim Paine as Australia's gloveman, receiving Baggy Green cap No.461 from Adam Gilchrist at the Gabba, with a maiden ton coming following summer at the Boxing Day Test against South Africa.

In a battle with Josh Inglis for the role of gloveman for Australia's white-ball teams, Carey remained a mainstay of the Test team. He famously stumped Jonny Bairstow during the 2023 Ashes Test at Lord's when the Englishman wandered out of his crease off the bowling of Cameron Green.

In a purple patch with the bat throughout the 2024-25 summer and beyond, Carey scored a century in the Sheffield Shield final as South Australia broke their title drought in March 2025.

players.name: Beau Webster
players.bio:
Raised in the small town of Snug in southern Tasmania, Webster burst into state ranks with dominant performances in the Tasmanian Premier League.

A prospective AFL draftee, Webster played for the Tassie Mariners at the under-18 level before choosing the cricket path. At only 20, Webster amassed 677 runs at 45.13 for his local side Kingborough and was awarded a Tigers rookie contract in 2013-14.

After impressing with 494 runs including two centuries in his first full Sheffield Shield season in 2015-16, Webster's watershed moment came in the Covid winter of 2020 when he shifted from a part-time off-spinner to a fully-fledged pace-bowling allrounder.

Four years later, the right-hander produced one of the greatest individual Shield seasons of all-time to lead the Tigers back to the final after a fifth-placed finish the season prior.

Webster's 938 runs, 30 wickets and 24 catches in 2023-24 saw him become just the second player to score 900 runs and take 30 wickets in the Shield's 131-year history (after Garry Sobers' 973 runs and 47 wickets for South Australia in 1963-64).

Webster was called up for his Test debut in the fifth and final Test of the blockbuster 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy series, handed Baggy Green No.469 by Australian great Mark Waugh at the Sydney Cricket Ground. He delivered with a vital half-century in Australia's win. He was also Australia's best performer with the bat at the ICC World Test Championship Final against South Africa in 2025.

players.name: Pat Cummins
players.didyouKnow: Named player of the match in his Test debut against South Africa in Johannesburg in 2011, Cummins claimed 6-79 in the second innings and hit the winni
players.bio:
Having burst onto the scene as a 17-year-old who topped the wicket-taker list in the 2010-11 state-based Big Bash League, Pat Cummins was quickly identified as a future star.

Soon enough in 2011-12, the Sydney boy became the youngest player ever to earn a central contract with Cricket Australia.

On the back of just a handful of first-class games, he was thrown into the deep end of Test cricket against South Africa in 2011. Showing no signs of nerves, he took 6-79 in the second innings and hit the winning runs to be named player of the match in Australia's narrow win.

After a long run of injuries, Cummins returned to the NSW side for the Marsh One-Day Cup and was part of the Australian squad that won the 2015 ODI World-Cup.

After careful management and working his way back to full fitness in shorter forms of the game, Cummins became a Test fixture from the 2017-18 Ashes onwards, spearheading an enviable pace attack alongside Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood.

He quickly rose to be the world's No.1 ranked bowler in Test cricket, and was part of the side that won Australia's first ever men's T20 World Cup in 2021.

In November 2021, just days out from the opening Test of that summer's Ashes series, Pat Cummins became Australia's 47th Test captain.

He was then appointed the nation's 27th men's ODI skipper in 2022, leading Australia back to the pinnacle a year later in what some have lauded as the nation's greatest World Cup triumph with a flawless captaincy and bowling performance to defeat India in the final to silence the 100,000-strong home crowd in Ahmedabad.

players.name: Mitchell Starc
players.didyouKnow: Starc began his under-age career as a wicketkeeper before being convinced to abandon the gloves and turn to fast bowling.
players.bio:
On track to finish his career as one of Australia's all-time greatest fast bowlers, Mitchell Starc's classical left-arm action and ability to swing the ball at pace has made him one of the most watchable players of the modern era.

Hailing from NSW, Starc made his international debut aged 20 and announced himself in just his second international match, taking 4-27 in an ODI against Sri Lanka at the Gabba in 2010.

A Test debut followed in 2011, and in the next summer Starc took eight wickets for the match against South Africa in Perth before bowling Australia to victory against Sri Lanka in Hobart, taking 5-63.

Australia's title-winning 2015 World Cup campaign brought out the very best in him – he was deservedly named player of the tournament for his tally of 22 wickets, and his first-over dismissal of Brendan McCullum in the final is one of his most famous wickets.

In November 2017, Starc became the first bowler to take a hat-trick in each innings of a Sheffield Shield match, while playing for New South Wales against Western Australia.

His 200th Test scalp came in February 2019, securing his spot alongside some of the greats of the game, while his 300th came against South Africa in late 2022.

That year, Starc became the quickest ever bowler to 200 one-day international wickets, eclipsing a 23-year benchmark set by off-spinner Saqlain Mushtaq.

He added another ODI World Cup title in 2023, taking 16 wickets to cement himself as one of the tournament's most prolific bowlers of all time, and was part of the side that won Australia's first ever men's T20 World Cup in 2021.

He joined the elite in 2025, taking his 400th Test wicket in his 100th Test match in the Caribbean in July.

Starc retired from T20 International cricket with 79 wickets from 65 games in September 2025 to focus on extending his Test and ODI careers, targetting the 2027 triple treat of a Border-Gavaskar Trophy tour of India, an ODI World Cup in South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe and, of course, an Ashes tour.

He valiantly led Australia's pace attack in the 2025-26 Ashes series without an injured Josh Hazlewood and Pat Cummins only able to play one match. He was player of the match in the opening two Tests, had two seven-wicket hauls and finished the series with 31 wickets at 19.93 to be awarded the Compton-Miller Medal as player of the series.

players.name: Josh Hazlewood
players.didyouKnow: Hazlewood was only 17 when he first represented NSW in 2008, making him the youngest ever fast-bowler to play for the state.
players.bio:
A country boy from near Tamworth known as the 'Bendemeer Bullet', Hazlewood became the youngest ever fast-bowler to represent New South Wales in 2008, aged just 17.

An international debut followed in 2010, aged 19, when he took on England in an ODI in Southampton, becoming the youngest Australian player at that level.

Often compared to his idol Glenn McGrath, Hazlewood has forged a career on metronomic accuracy outside off stump with steep bounce due to both a large 196cm frame and a high release.

Forming one-third of a fearsome attack featuring Pat Cummins and Mitchell Starc, Hazlewood has long been one of Australia's first-picked players in Test and ODI cricket, however until 2020 this did not extend to the game's shortest format.

But huge improvements to his variations and off-pace deliveries saw Hazlewood become a key member of Chennai Super Kings' 2021 IPL triumph and, later that year, Australia's maiden T20 World Cup title, sealing his reputation as one of the world's premier all-format bowlers.

Hazlewood was a key member of Australia's historic ODI World Cup triumph in 2023 and passed 250 Test wickets in the summer that followed, seeing him enter the top 10 wicket-takers for Australia in history.

players.name: Aiden Markram
players.bio:
Aiden Markram is a talented opening batter from Northerns and he became the first South African captain to win a World Cup, albeit at under age level (2014 Under-19 World Cup).

He made his Test debut in 2017, falling just short of a century with 97 against Bangladesh in Potchefstroom. He first Test series against Australia was a raging success too, scoring two tons (143 and 152) as South Africa won the 2018 series 3-1.

Dropped from the Test side in 2022, Markram returned to the side in 2023 and cemented his spot with hundreds against West Indies and India. 

Markram has captained his country in both white-ball formats and is a handy off-spinner and fielder.

players.name: Marques Ackerman
players.bio: Marques Ackerman is a left-handed batter from Johannesburg who made his Test debut against Australia in the second Test of the 2026 series at St George's Park, Gqeberha.

players.name: David Bedingham
players.bio:
Considered somewhat of a Test specialist, it took years and years of churning out domestic runs in South Africa and England before David Bedingham got a look at the top level. 

A well-organised and technically sound right-handed batter, Bedingham's time came when he made his debut against India in the Boxing Day Test in 2023.

players.name: Temba Bavuma
players.bio:
Temba Bavuma made his first-class debut for Gauteng at just 18 and three years later made his debut for South Africa A.

His maiden Test century came in 2016, where he made an unbeaten 102 against England. And Bavuma would find his feet at international level. Between 2021 and 2024 Bavuma scored 1,584 Test runs at an average of 48, while also building a solid ODI record. 

He took the reins of the Test side following Dean Elgar's retirement in 2023 and led South Africa to a semi-final at the ODI World Cup the same year.

players.name: Ryan Rickelton
players.bio:
A flashy left-handed batter, Ryan Rickelton was 25 when he made his Test debut against Bangladesh in 2022. 

While it took him a couple of years to cement his place in the side, Rickelton was instrumental in South Africa's run to the 2023-25 WTC Final with scores of 101 against Sri Lanka and 259 against Pakistan in important victories. 

A strong season for MI Cape Town in the SA20 league saw Rickelton earn an IPL contract with Mumbai Indians, scoring 388 in 2025.

players.name: Wiaan Mulder
players.bio:
A genuine allrounder, Wiaan Mulder was a constant figure in South Africa's underage sides growing up. 

He made his ODI debut at the age of 19 in 2017 but was never able to solidify his position in any of the international formats. That was until the 2023-25 WTC cycle, where Mulder's contributions with the bat and handy wickets made him a vital cog in South Africa's run to the final.

players.name: Marco Jansen
players.bio:
A left armer who can swing the ball both ways, Marco Jansen also stands at over 2m tall. 

Jansen was only 21 when he made his Test debut and had his first Test five-wicket haul less than a year later when he claimed 5-35 against England at the Oval. 

In late 2024 he took a barely believable 7-13 against Sri Lanka in Durban as the visitors were bowled out for 42. 

Jansen is an all-format player for South Africa and is more than handy with the bat too, with multiple half-centuries already under his belt.

players.name: Kagiso Rabada
players.didyouKnow: Originally played rugby before switching to cricket.
players.bio:
Kagiso Rabada made his Proteas debut in a T20I against Australia in Adelaide at just 19.

Rabada was one of the stars of the South Africa team who won their maiden ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup in 2014, claiming 6-25 in the semi-final against Australia in a man-of-the-match performance.

The fast bowler made his first class debut in March 2014 and the selectors were quickly impressed, granting him a Test debut in 2015.

Adapting quickly to the highest level, Rabada took a seven-wicket haul in the first-innings against England at Centurion in just his fifth Test. 

In his first Test series against Australia, the spearhead took 11-150 in the Gqeberha Test as South Africa won the match and levelled the series. 

In 2024, Rabada became just the sixth South African to take 300 Test wickets, all while maintaining a strike rate below 40 and an average below 23.
